title: Building an AI Voice Agent for 360 Degree Feedback: How Your360 AI Uses State Machines, Evals, and Layered Synthesis
text: Building an AI Voice Agent for 360 Degree Feedback: How Your360 AI Uses State Machines, Evals, and Layered Synthesis Our Courses Train Your Team Articles Just Now Possible Get in Touch Sign in Subscribe Building an AI Voice Agent for 360 Degree Feedback: How Your360 AI Uses State Machines, Evals, and Layered Synthesis Teresa Torres 15 Oct 2026 53 min Listen to this episode on: Spotify | Apple Podcasts What does it take to build an AI voice agent that people will talk to for 44 minutes about their own blind spots? Your360 AI found out, one call at a time. In this episode of Just Now Possible , Teresa Torres talks with Jared Goralnick (Co-Founder and CEO), Eda Goksel Jackson (Head of Design), and Alex Krasun (AI Engineer) at Your360 AI. Their product brings interview-based 360 degree feedback, once reserved for the C-suite, to anyone. A voice AI coach named Tam runs the self-discovery call, interviews each feedback provider, and walks the recipient through their report. They get specific about what it took: replacing a single prompt with state machines so Tam doesn't lose the thread, moving from Retell to LiveKit to control every layer of a cascading voice stack, and running AI evals with personas built from calls that failed. Then comes the hard part: synthesis that is accurate, corroborated, and genuinely anonymous. You'll hear how they balance observability against sensitive data, why reasoning models are a poor fit for voice, and how structural and substantive eval passes catch both outright mistakes and missed patterns. Show Notes Guests Jared Goralnick, Co-Founder and CEO, Your360 AI Eda Goksel Jackson, Head of Design, Your360 AI Alex Krasun, AI Engineer, Your360 AI Key Takeaways They built the product one call at a time. The self-discovery agent shipped and was validated a month before feedback collection existed, and synthesis came after that. A single prompt couldn't hold a structured conversation. State machines keep the agent on track while still letting it go deep when someone wants to. Voice AI is not a survey. People answer three questions in their first sentence, so the agent has to track what has already been covered and decide when to push and when to move on. If a customer won't let you look at conversations in the early days, that tells you something about the market. Find design partners who will, then build automated flags so humans only step in when something goes wrong. Synthesis needs two kinds of evals. Structural passes catch "don't mess up" errors like misattributed feedback. Substantive passes re-run the analysis with few rules to find patterns the first pass missed.
